about: The console families oldipmi-core supports, for the desktop: the C++ code (desktop/families.cpp) and the QML (qml/families.js) read this table, and the Go tests of internal/backend check it against the core's driver registry (drivers.go) and the pictures (desktop/images/family-<id>.png). id is stored in the profile; name, short and hint are what the connection dialog, the list and the console pane show. account: the family needs a username and password (false: neither, and no wallet entry). consoleMode, jnlp and clientCertificate: the advanced options the connection dialog offers (the console mode, the JNLP endpoint override, the client certificate). synthetic: no hardware behind it (the demo console); the welcome page and the core's message for an unknown family leave it out.

families.name: Supermicro (ATEN)
families.hint: Supermicro X9 and newer, and most X8 boards. Uses the Java iKVM protocol or the HTML5 console, whichever the firmware offers.

families.name: AMI MegaRAC
families.hint: AMI MegaRAC firmware, including Supermicro X8 boards that shipped with it (e.g. X8DTU), and ASUS, Tyan or Gigabyte BMCs.

families.name: Dell iDRAC (Avocent)
families.hint: Dell PowerEdge 12th generation and older with an Avocent-based iDRAC 6/7 virtual console.

families.name: Cisco IMC
families.hint: Cisco UCS C-Series Integrated Management Controller (Avocent-based KVM).

families.name: Demo console (no hardware)
families.hint: A synthetic console that echoes keys, pointer and clicks. For trying OldIPMI and testing AI agents without a BMC. Address "demo", or e.g. "demo-1920x1080".
